title: Blended learning in the context of digitalization
reason: Re-extraction (inclusion not re-decided). Descriptive case study: counts of Moodle registration, guest access, task completion by level and forum use are read as DigComp levels. No statistical indicator-outcome relation; personality constructs absent. Would likely fail I1-I4; flagged.

extraction.country: Ukraine (Vocational College of Oleksandr Dovzhenko Hlukhiv National Pedagogical University)
extraction.design: descriptive case study (trial implementation of blended learning; counts and percentages)
extraction.n_quote: 59 students of different ages were involved in the study.
extraction.population: future masters of industrial training in sewing, vocational college of a pedagogical university
extraction.lms_indicators: Moodle self-registration success, use of 'Guest access', percentage of tasks completed at reproductive/interpretive/creative levels, forum and e-mail communication, Google Meet use
extraction.outcome_or_construct: digital competence level (DigComp 2.1 areas 1, 2, 5) inferred by the authors from the same activity counts
extraction.notes: Table 2 cells: country Ukraine and LMS indicators confirmed; design is descriptive rather than quasi-experimental (no comparison group, no test); n = 59 now recoverable. No effect size can exist: the competence levels are assigned from the activity counts themselves (e.g. 'at least 8 out of 30 people (26.6%) ... met the criteria of the third level of DigComp'), so indicator and construct are not independently measured. Sub-counts use inconsistent bases (30, 36, 59; 40 students = 41.6% implies ~96). Vocational-college sample satisfies E3.
